subject: medicine
title: Membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis, tram-tracking, and Alport syndrome

steps.tx: Chronic immune deposition and complement dysregulation stimulate exuberant mesangial expansion combined with capillary loop remodeling. Pathologically designated as **membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis** (MPGN), this pattern of glomerular injury features marked mesangial cellular proliferation, increased mesangial matrix deposition, and circumferential interposition of mesangial cell processes into the peripheral capillary walls. Patients typically present with a mixed nephritic-nephrotic phenotype, exhibiting persistent haematuria, heavy proteinuria, systemic hypertension, and progressive decline in renal filtration clearance over a prolonged course.
steps.say: Chronic immune deposition and complement dysregulation stimulate mesangial expansion and capillary loop remodelling. Pathologically designated as membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis, this injury features mesangial proliferation and interposition of cell processes into capillary walls. Patients present with a mixed nephritic-nephrotic picture, featuring haematuria, hypertension, and progressive renal insufficiency.

vis.caption: Lobular accentuation, mesangial hypercellularity, and capillary wall thickening in MPGN. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Circumferential interposition of mesangial cellular extensions into subendothelial capillary spaces alters basement membrane contour on special histological staining. Demonstrating a **tram-track appearance** (double-contour basement membrane duplication) on silver methenamine or periodic acid-Schiff staining reveals splitting of the capillary wall. As interposed mesangial cells migrate between the endothelial cell and the native basement membrane, they synthesize new subendothelial extracellular matrix material. This produces parallel inner and outer lamina densa lines visible on high-power light and electron microscopy.
steps.say: Interposition of mesangial cell extensions into subendothelial spaces affects basement membrane contour on special stains. Demonstrating a tram-track appearance on silver stains reveals characteristic splitting of the capillary wall. As mesangial cells migrate along the capillary loop, they synthesize new basement membrane material, creating parallel lines on microscopy.

steps.tx: Contemporary reclassification of membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis stratifies cases according to underlying molecular immunofluorescence pathways rather than legacy ultrastructural numbering. Developing the **modern MPGN classification** separates immunoglobulin-mediated disease from pure complement-mediated C3 glomerulopathy. Immunoglobulin-positive MPGN features granular IgG or IgM with complement, driven by chronic hepatitis C infection with cryoglobulinaemia, autoimmune disorders, or monoclonal gammopathies. Conversely, complement-dominant C3 glomerulopathy (including dense deposit disease and C3 glomerulonephritis) results from acquired C3 nephritic factor autoantibodies or genetic alternative pathway dysregulation.
steps.say: Modern classification of membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis stratifies cases by immunofluorescence staining rather than outdated numbers. Developing the modern MPGN classification separates immunoglobulin-driven disease from pure complement-mediated C3 glomerulopathy. Immunoglobulin-positive disease associates with hepatitis C or monoclonal gammopathies, whereas C3 glomerulopathy arises from alternative complement pathway dysregulation.

steps.tx: Inherited structural abnormalities of basement membrane collagen networks produce progressive renal, auditory, and ocular pathology. Inherited as an X-linked dominant condition in eighty-five percent of cases, **Alport syndrome** results from loss-of-function mutations in the COL4A5 gene on the X chromosome, encoding the alpha-five chain of type four collagen. Defective alpha-three-four-five collagen heterotrimers destabilize basement membranes across the glomerulus, cochlea, and lens capsule. Patients present in childhood with persistent microscopic haematuria, developing bilateral high-frequency sensorineural deafness, anterior lenticonus, perimacular retinal flecks, and progressive renal failure.
steps.say: Inherited structural abnormalities of basement membrane collagen networks cause progressive renal, auditory, and ocular disease. Inherited as an X-linked dominant trait, Alport syndrome results from mutations in the COL4A5 gene encoding type four collagen. Defective collagen trimers destabilize membranes across the glomerulus, cochlea, and lens, producing haematuria, high-frequency deafness, and anterior lenticonus.

vis.alt: Diagram showing type IV collagen alpha chains and clinical triad of Alport syndrome.
vis.caption: Type IV collagen alpha-chain defect, basket-weave lamina densa, and Alport syndrome triad. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Ultrastructural examination under electron microscopy provides definitive confirmation of hereditary collagenous basement membrane breakdown. Observing diagnostic **basket-weave lamellation** on electron microscopy reveals irregular thickening, thinning, splitting, and longitudinal multidirectional lamellation of the lamina densa within the glomerular basement membrane. Intervening lucent areas contain fine granular proteinaceous debris. This irregular fragmentation contrasts sharply with thin basement membrane nephropathy (benign familial haematuria), which features diffuse, uniform attenuation of the basement membrane below two hundred and fifty nanometres without structural lamellation.
steps.say: Ultrastructural examination using electron microscopy provides definitive confirmation of hereditary basement membrane breakdown. Observing diagnostic basket-weave lamellation reveals irregular thickening, thinning, and longitudinal splitting of the lamina densa. This structural disruption contrasts sharply with thin basement membrane disease, which features uniform thinning without fragmentation.

points: Basket-weave multidirectional splitting of lamina densa

Involves COL4A5 mutation with progressive renal decline

right.title: Thin Basement Membrane Disease
points: Uniform, diffuse thinning of basement membrane (<250 nm)
Pristine lamina densa without splitting or lamellation

steps.tx: Microscopic identification of cylindrical cellular aggregates in urinary sediment localizes haematuria definitively to active glomerular inflammation. Identifying **red cell casts** on fresh urine sediment examination provides absolute confirmation of glomerular bleeding. Formed when dysmorphic erythrocytes (including pathognomonic ring-shaped acanthocytes with bleb-like protrusions) pass through disrupted glomerular capillary walls, they become entrapped within Tamm-Horsfall mucoprotein gel matrices secreted by thick ascending limb cells. Red cell casts readily degenerate into pigmented brownish-orange heme granular casts under conditions of aciduria and tubular stasis.
steps.say: Microscopic identification of cylindrical cellular aggregates in urine localizes bleeding definitively to active glomerular inflammation. Identifying red cell casts on fresh sediment examination provides absolute confirmation of glomerular bleeding. Formed when dysmorphic erythrocytes pass through broken capillary walls, they become trapped within Tamm-Horsfall mucoprotein matrices in the distal tubules.

rows: Definitive pathognomonic marker of active glomerulonephritis
Glomerular mechanical deformation and osmotic lysis

steps.tx: Percutaneous tissue sampling under real-time ultrasound guidance represents the definitive diagnostic procedure in unexplained parenchymal renal disease. Directing a **renal biopsy** is formally indicated in unexplained acute kidney injury, nephrotic syndrome in adults, active systemic lupus erythematosus with renal involvement, and rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis. Strict pre-procedure safety criteria mandate normal coagulation parameters (INR under one point two, platelet count above one hundred thousand), normal bleeding time, well-controlled blood pressure below one hundred and forty over ninety, and verification of two functional kidneys on imaging.
steps.say: Percutaneous tissue sampling under real-time ultrasound guidance represents the definitive diagnostic procedure in parenchymal kidney disease. Directing a renal biopsy is indicated in unexplained acute kidney injury, adult nephrotic syndrome, and rapidly progressive nephritis. Strict pre-procedure safety criteria require normal coagulation parameters, well-controlled blood pressure, and two functioning kidneys on imaging.

Ultrasound-Guided Automated Needle Core Biopsy -> Tripartite Processing

steps.tx: Comprehensive histopathological interpretation of percutaneous core tissue requires division into three distinct specimen aliquots for specialized processing. Completing **biopsy tissue processing** allocates tissue to light microscopy (fixed in formalin and stained with haematoxylin and eosin, PAS for basement membranes, Masson trichrome for interstitial fibrosis, and Jones silver for capillary loop details). A second fresh frozen core undergoes immunofluorescence staining for immunoglobulins (IgG, IgA, IgM) and complement fractions (C3, C1q). A third core is fixed in glutaraldehyde for electron microscopic ultrastructural analysis.
steps.say: Comprehensive histopathological interpretation of renal biopsy cores requires division into three distinct specimen aliquots. Completing biopsy tissue processing allocates tissue to light microscopy with special silver and trichrome stains. A second frozen core undergoes immunofluorescence staining for antibodies and complement, while a third core enters glutaraldehyde for electron microscopic ultrastructural analysis.
